extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and substantive guidance on abandonment, petitions to withdraw a holding of abandonment, petitions to revive abandoned applications, refunds tied to express abandonment, and related timing, evidentiary, and form requirements under the MPEP and relevant CFR provisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Refund under 37 CFR 1.138(d) (express abandonment before examination)
rubrics_metrics.description: Refund of the search fee and excess claims fee paid in an application filed under 35 U.S.C. 111(a) and 37 CFR 1.53(b) on or after Dec. 8, 2004 may be obtained by submitting a petition and declaration of express abandonment before an examination has been made of the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A petition under 37 CFR 1.138(d) will be granted only if filed before an examination has been made; denied if not. If a petition and declaration of express abandonment are not filed before an examination has been made, the Office may retain the entire search fee and excess claims fee. The Office recommends submission via PTO/SB/24B (or PTO/AIA/24B). A two-month refund-request filing period is referenced elsewhere but is not extendable when associated with other filing deadlines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'examination has been made of the application' for 1.138(d)
rubrics_metrics.description: An 'examination has been made of the application' once an action (e.g., restriction/election requirement, requirement for information under 37 CFR 1.105, first Office action on the merits, notice of allowability/allowance, action under Ex parte Quayle) is shown in the One Patent Service Gateway as having been counted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For purposes of 1.138(d), 'before' means earlier in time; if a petition is filed and an action is counted on the same day, the petition was not filed before examination. The date on any certificate of mailing or transmission under 37 CFR 1.8 is not taken into account in determining whether a petition under 1.138(d) was filed before an examination.

rubrics_metrics.name: PDP/One Patent Service Gateway status check for petition timeliness
rubrics_metrics.description: The Patent Data Portal (PDP) shows status codes; if the PDP status is higher than 031 before or on the day the petition under 37 CFR 1.138(d) was filed, the petition will be denied.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The PDP system maintains computerized content records and will show a status higher than 031 once an action has been counted. Petitioners should check PDP/Patent Center status to confirm that no action has been counted prior to filing the petition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effectiveness of petition under 1.138(d) to stop publication
rubrics_metrics.description: A petition under 37 CFR 1.138(d) may not be effective to stop publication unless the petition is granted and the abandonment processed before technical preparations for publication have begun.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Technical preparations for publication generally begin four months prior to the projected date of publication; filing the petition late in that window may not prevent publication even if the petition is ultimately granted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Forms for filing express abandonment and related petitions
rubrics_metrics.description: Form PTO/AIA/24 (or PTO/SB/24), PTO/AIA/24A (or PTO/SB/24A), and PTO/AIA/24B (or PTO/SB/24B) may be used for filing a letter of express abandonment, a petition for express abandonment to avoid publication (1.138(c)), or a petition for express abandonment to obtain a refund (1.138(d)), respectively.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Office recommends using the USPTO electronic filing system and the specified forms reproduced in MPEP § 711.01 subsection V. Use the form appropriate to the filing date (pre- or post-AIA).

rubrics_metrics.name: Abandonment for failure to reply within statutory period (37 CFR 1.135(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: An application becomes abandoned if applicant 'fails to reply' to an Office action within the fixed statutory period, either by failing to reply within the statutory period or by filing an insufficient reply (failure to file a 'complete and proper reply').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiners must know the dates that mark the beginning and end of the statutory period under varying situations. Applicant's reply is considered timely if filed within the shortened statutory period, full statutory period, or within extended time obtained under 37 CFR 1.136. If an amendment is filed after expiration and is not timely under 35 U.S.C. 21 and 37 CFR 1.7, the application is abandoned and remedy is petition to revive. Examiner should notify applicant using Notice of Abandonment form PTOL-1432 and appropriate form paragraphs (e.g., 7.90, 7.98.02).

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirements for petition to revive under 37 CFR 1.137 (unintentional delay)
rubrics_metrics.description: A petition to revive an abandoned application on the grounds that the failure to reply was unintentional must be accompanied by (1) the required reply, (2) a statement that the entire delay was unintentional, (3) any required terminal disclaimer, and (4) the petition fee set forth in 37 CFR 1.17(m).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No consideration to substance of a petition will be given until the fee is received. The Director may require additional information where there is question whether the delay was unintentional. Specific reply content requirements vary by the reason for abandonment (see 1.137(c)); revival of certain application types (design, pre-1995 utility/plant) may require terminal disclaimers as per 1.137(d).

rubrics_metrics.name: Limits on extension periods and fully responsive reply requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The date on which a petition under 37 CFR 1.136(a) and the appropriate extension fee have been filed is the operative date for determining the period and fee. In no case may an applicant reply outside the SIX (6) MONTH statutory period or obtain an extension for more than FIVE (5) MONTHS beyond the date for reply set forth in an Office action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A fully responsive reply must be timely filed to avoid abandonment. If the reply appears to be a bona fide attempt with an inadvertent omission, use form paragraph 7.95 instead of form paragraph 7.91. Examiner notes should identify why a reply is not fully responsive.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special situations that may result in abandonment
rubrics_metrics.description: Various particular circumstances often give rise to questions of abandonment and should be specially noted (examples A–H): copying claims from a patent, withdrawal/failure to prosecute appeals, dismissal of appeals, claims suggested for interference near the end of reply period, filing CPAs, improperly filed RCEs, filing an RCE without timely submission when reply to final action outstanding, and RCEs filed prior to payment of issue fee without appropriate fee or submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each situation has particular consequences: e.g., copying claims from a patent not suggested by the Office does not constitute a reply (unless the last Office action relied solely on the patent); an improper RCE may be treated as a withdrawal of appeal and will not toll prior time periods. See cited MPEP sections for details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Termination of proceedings (35 U.S.C. 120 context)
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Termination of proceedings' means a second application is considered copending with an earlier application if it is filed before (A) patenting, (B) abandonment of, or (C) termination of proceedings on the earlier application; 'before' interpreted to mean 'not later than.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proceedings are terminated in specified situations (e.g., abandonment for failure to pay issue fee, losing an interference as to all claims, decision by PTAB or court). See MPEP § 711.03(b) for examples and dates that determine termination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reconsideration of a holding of abandonment vs revival
rubrics_metrics.description: An applicant may ask for reconsideration of a holding of abandonment if they disagree that abandonment occurred (e.g., disagreement as to sufficiency of reply or controlling dates), or may petition for revival under 37 CFR 1.137.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The primary examiner can reverse a holding as to whether an amendment received was responsive and act on an application previously held abandoned (this is not a revival). Where there is no dispute as to dates, no reconsideration can be presented. A petition under 1.181(a) to withdraw the holding of abandonment is appropriate and requires no fee; a petition under 1.137 (to revive) requires the petition fee.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 CFR 1.181 petitions to the Director (procedural limits)
rubrics_metrics.description: Petitions under 37 CFR 1.181 may be taken to the Director from any action or requirement of an examiner not subject to appeal to PTAB, in cases the statute/rules specify Director review, or to invoke supervisory authority; the mere filing of a petition does not stay any period for reply and petitions not filed within two months of the mailing date of the action may be dismissed as untimely.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any petition under this part not filed within two months of the action or notice may be dismissed as untimely except as provided. The two-month period is not extendable. For petitions involving PTAB actions, see § 41.3.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition to withdraw holding of abandonment (when appropriate)
rubrics_metrics.description: Where applicant contends the application is not abandoned (e.g., dispute as to sufficiency of reply or controlling dates), a petition under 37 CFR 1.181(a) requesting withdrawal of the holding of abandonment is appropriate and does not require a fee; where there is no dispute as to abandonment, a petition under 37 CFR 1.137 (with fee) is necessary to revive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Petition type depends on whether there's an actual dispute about abandonment. The petition to withdraw (1.181) may be used to ask the examiner/Director to withdraw a holding; revival (1.137) is used where abandonment is conceded but relief is sought.

rubrics_metrics.name: Showing of nonreceipt required of a practitioner to withdraw holding
rubrics_metrics.description: A practitioner alleging nonreceipt of an Office communication must submit a statement describing the system used for recording received Office actions at the correspondence address of record, establishing the docketing system is sufficiently reliable, and include records such as master docket, application file jacket, incoming mail log, calendar, reminder system, or individual docket records.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The statement should show the Office action was not received and provide documentary proof (application number, attorney docket number, mail date, due date). If no master docket exists, other firm records should be provided. Showing must be credible; a history of 'not receiving Office actions' may undermine the claim.

rubrics_metrics.name: Showing of nonreceipt required of a pro se applicant
rubrics_metrics.description: A pro se petitioner must explain how they receive and track USPTO mail, maintain files for patent matters, where correspondence is kept, how due dates are recorded, and provide documentary evidence covering a reasonable period after the mailing date to demonstrate non-receipt.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pro se must explain reminders and record-keeping used, provide any available documents (e.g., file outsides, calendar entries), include a statement that a search was conducted and action not found, and state petitioner resided at/checked the correspondence address for a reasonable time after mailing date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition to withdraw based on timely mailing/filing evidence (Priority Mail Express®, postcard receipt, certificate of mailing)
rubrics_metrics.description: Petitioners may rely on timeliness showing via Priority Mail Express® procedures (37 CFR 1.10), postcard receipts (prima facie evidence), or certificates of mailing under 37 CFR 1.8 (with statement of personal knowledge or supporting evidence).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When relying on Priority Mail Express®, submit appropriate petition under 1.10(c),(d),(e),(g) and enter the paper in Patent Data Portal with the Priority Mail Express® date. Postcard receipt evidence must identify the reply and will result in entry using the postcard receipt date. Certificates of mailing under 1.8 require the attesting statement on personal knowledge or supporting evidence (mailing logs etc.) and the correspondence is entered with the actual date of receipt as shown on the duplicate copy filed with the 1.8 statement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of untimely petition to withdraw holding of abandonment (37 CFR 1.181(f))
rubrics_metrics.description: Any petition to withdraw the holding of abandonment not filed within two months from the mail date of the action complained of may be dismissed as untimely. Rather than dismissing, the Office may require a terminal disclaimer as a condition of granting an untimely petition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If record indicates applicant intentionally delayed filing the petition, the Office may dismiss it solely on that basis. Intentional delay precludes relief under 37 CFR 1.137. The two-month period is generally not extendable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequences and terminal disclaimer requirements for untimely petitions (application-type and receipt-dependent rules)
rubrics_metrics.description: For design applications, utilities filed before June 8, 1995, and plant applications filed before June 8, 1995: a petition to withdraw not filed within two months of the mail date of notice of abandonment will not be treated on the merits (absent extraordinary circumstances) unless accompanied by a terminal disclaimer under 37 CFR 1.321(a) and the fee; where applicant never received the notice, the period is twelve months from applicant’s filing/submission of correspondence before the petition will be treated on the merits without a terminal disclaimer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The period to be disclaimed equals the terminal part of the term of any patent equivalent to the period between (A) two months after mail date of notice of abandonment and (B) filing date of a grantable petition to withdraw (if notice received). If notice never received, the disclaimed period runs from twelve months from applicant's filing/submission of correspondence to filing date of a grantable petition. See MPEP § 711.03(c) subsection II.G for specifics. Different date windows and disclaimer requirements apply by application filing-date cohorts (e.g., pre-1995, post-1995).

rubrics_metrics.name: Revival options and special-case revival requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Revival may be sought under 37 CFR 1.137 for unintentional delay, and certain revivals (design, pre-June 8 1995 utility/plant) require a terminal disclaimer dedicating a terminal part of any patent term equivalent to the period of abandonment or the lesser of abandonment period or period extending beyond twenty years from earliest filing date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Petition must include required reply, fees, terminal disclaimer if applicable, and statement of unintentional delay. Revival can apply to provisional applications (subject to 12-month pendency limits) and to abandonment for failure to notify the Office of a foreign filing (notification meets reply requirement but revival won't stay other running reply periods). The Director may require additional info where delay intent is in question.
